does: Pours beaten egg into very hot oil in a wok so that it puffs at once, then pushes it into large, soft, fluffy curds that are taken out while still a little wet.
how: Beat the eggs with a little salt.
Heat the wok until it smokes, then add a good spoonful of oil and swirl it.
Pour in the eggs; they puff and bubble at the edges at once.
Push the set edges into the middle with a spatula so that the runny egg flows out, in a few large folds.
Take the curds out while they are still glossy and a little runny, and return them at the end.

cues.text: A loud sizzle as the egg hits the oil.
Large, puffy, golden-edged curds, still glossy in places.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring the eggs into a wok that is not hot enough, so they turn flat and rubbery.
mistakes.fix: Heat the wok and the oil until they shimmer.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking the eggs dry before taking them out.
mistakes.fix: Take them out while still a little runny; they cook again when they go back in.

variant_of.differs: High heat and plenty of oil make large, fluffy curds in moments, instead of small creamy ones over low heat.
